title.en: The last days and the sparrows' tribute

heading.en: Five years abroad, one last song

hook.en: When the author left for five years abroad, his grandmother did not cry. When he came back, she did something she had never done before.

objectives.en: Describe the farewell and the homecoming
Explain the circumstances of the grandmother's death
Interpret the sparrows and the main themes

narration.en: When the author left for five years abroad, his grandmother did not cry. When he came back, she did something she had never done before.

body.en: The grandmother came to the railway station to see him off. She did not show emotion; she was lost in prayer, telling her beads, and she kissed his forehead. The author treasured that moist imprint, thinking it might be their last contact. Five years later she was at the station to receive him, looking no older. That evening, for the first time, she did not say her prayers. She collected the women of the neighbourhood and, beating an old drum, sang for hours about warriors coming home.

points.en: Farewell: silent, praying, kisses his forehead
Return: she receives him at the station
Celebration: drum and songs; no prayers that evening

Let us place the final events on a timeline.

say.en: At the station she is silent and prayerful, and kisses his forehead.
The author studies abroad for five years.
She is at the station when he returns.
That evening she beats a drum and sings, and misses her prayers.
Next day she falls ill and prays silently.
She dies, and thousands of sparrows sit in silent mourning.

narration.en: The final part of the portrait, retold in our own words. Put the events in order.

prompt.en: Put the events of the grandmother's last days in order.

steps.en: She sees him off at the station, praying and silent
Five years later she is at the station to receive him
That evening she skips her prayers and sings with the neighbourhood women
Next morning she falls ill; the doctor calls the fever mild
Sure her end has come, she prays and refuses to talk
She dies peacefully, telling her beads
Thousands of sparrows sit silently around her body
They ignore the crumbs and fly away after the body is carried off

explanation.en: The silent sparrows are the most moving tribute: she had fed them every day.

body.en: The next morning she fell ill. The doctor said the fever was mild, but she was sure her end had come. Regretting the prayers she had missed, she refused to talk to anyone and lay in bed praying and telling her beads until she died peacefully. When the family went to carry her body for cremation, thousands of sparrows sat silently around it. They ignored the bread crumbs the author's mother threw them and flew away quietly only after the body was carried off.

points.en: She knew her end had come; she prayed till the last
Thousands of silent sparrows mourned her
Themes: love across generations, faith, loneliness with dignity

problem.en: What is the significance of the sparrows at the end of the story?

steps.en: She had fed the sparrows every afternoon in the city.
At her death they sat silently and refused the bread crumbs.
They left only when her body was carried away.

answer.en: The sparrows she had fed every day came to mourn her. Their silence and refusal to eat show that her love for living creatures was returned. Nature itself pays a final tribute to her gentle, loving spirit.

points.en: She bid the author a silent, prayerful farewell and welcomed him home with songs.
She sensed her end, prayed to the last and died peacefully.
The silent sparrows show how her love for all creatures was returned.
Themes: love across generations, faith, the generation gap and dignity in old age.
